result.family: F11 Lazy Pre-Norm — RMSNorm fused into a GEMM as a prologue (Zhou et al., PyTorch blog 2026-07-10 §2), applied to the two K=6144 consumers of post_attention_layernorm: (a) the routed-expert w13 grouped GEMM and (b) the router GEMM
result.verdict:
F11a (w13 grouped GEMM): DO NOT SHIP — clear, large regression. 0.90-0.97x at decode, 0.476x/0.603x at prefill, against a roofline ceiling of only 1.00-1.01x (expert-weight traffic of 0.37-12.9 GB swamps the 0.02-192 MB the fusion removes, so there was never headroom). Sum-of-squares redundancy is cdiv(4096,BLOCK_N) x top_k = 256-512x and it does NOT hide behind the MMA pipeline.

F11b (router GEMM): a genuine but small PREFILL-ONLY win — 1.096x (t2048) and 1.127x (t8192), i.e. 15%/20% of the 1.64x headroom; 0.68-0.77x at decode. Redundancy is only 2-8x here, which is why it can win at all. At t8192 the fused kernel's mapping optimum shifts to BLOCK_N=128 specifically to halve redundancy.

ATTRIBUTION (three independent measurements, all in the JSON). (i) Isolation — this fusion adds no extra input tensor, so timing FUSE_NORM on-vs-off at the identical config on identical buffers is an EXACT instruction-cost measurement (F1 needed a stride-0 broadcast to approximate what is exact here): w13 costs +1.0-1.2% where the GEMM is memory-bound but +65.0-67.7% where it is compute-bound; router +12.4-63.0%. The extra work does not overlap the MMA pipeline, it displaces it — the same shape as F1's codegen cliff. (ii) Matched-config sweeps from the recorded tune tables confirm the fused side is uniformly 1.12-3.30x slower at identical mappings, so it is not an under-tuned baseline artifact. (iii) Registers rise +26 to +28/thread with ZERO spills, and both variants still fit the same number of CTAs/SM at t2048 — so unlike F6 this is not an occupancy collapse. But there IS a hard SMEM bar: 7 of 79 coarse configs compile unfused and fail fused with exactly +4096 B over the limit (cross-warp reduction scratch), including BM128 BN128 BK64 w16 s2 — the tile family of the unfused winner at t8192. Third distinct toxic-fusion mechanism for the study.

WHY THE PAPER'S CLAIM DOESN'T PORT: the blog relies on warp specialization to put the reduction on dedicated warps; Triton 3.0 on MACA has none (no WS, no TMA, no clusters), so the free lane the algorithm needs does not exist. Four sum-of-squares implementations were compared (per-step tl.sum, tile-accumulate, tensor-core dot-with-ones, second-load) in a recorded pre-study — they move the cost by 10-30% and none removes it; which wins flips with BLOCK_N and with compute- vs bandwidth-boundedness. (Triton CSEs the two identical tl.loads, so mode 3 compiles to mode 0 and times identically to 0.1%.)

WHAT IS WORTH SHIPPING: the exploratory "half-fused" variant (rstd from a tiny reduction kernel, applied as a pure epilogue scale on an otherwise-untouched GEMM). It beats full lazy pre-norm on the router at EVERY regime (1.03-1.24x), never regresses there, and reaches 95-100% of its own roofline ceiling (1.241x at prefill). It captures 2 of the 3 activation passes the full fusion saves, with none of the mainloop cost, and composes better since one rstd kernel serves all consumers. Conclusion: on C500/Triton 3.0 normalization is not free, and the closest to free is to stop putting it inside the k-loop.

SIDE FINDINGS: (a) GLM-5.2's affine RMSNorm weight is NOT a blocker at inference — folding w into B's rows offline costs nothing at runtime and validates to 2.9e-03; (b) the fused path is MORE accurate than the framework path (1.5e-03 vs 2.5e-03 vs an exact fp32 reference) because it skips the bf16 rounding of x2 — but it flips ~1.2% of top-8 routing decisions on near-ties, so F11b is not a bit-exact drop-in; (c) vendor BLAS reaches 200-224 TF/s on the dense-equivalent w13 shape vs our best Triton grouped GEMM at 86.7 TF/s, but the vendor's per-expert matmul loop (20.10 ms at t2048) LOSES to our unfused Triton grouped GEMM (13.83 ms).
result.issues:
1) x2 materialization: took option (ii) — ALL K==6144 consumers fused, so x2 is genuinely dead and never written. Stated as an explicit precondition in the kernel docstring, the bench docstring, the JSON (x2_materialization.choice) and the log; the shared expert would need the same treatment (identical transform on a 1-expert weight). Because glm52/traffic.py charges the same norm kernel to F11a AND F11b (double-counting it), a third "combined" row is reported that charges ONE norm kernel to the unfused side — that is the honest end-to-end number.

2) Grid symmetry: coarse grids are IDENTICAL config lists on both sides at every regime (router 30/30, 64/64, 116/116; w13 99/99, 79/79) — the generator takes no `fused` argument because, unlike F6, the lazy-prenorm kernel stages no extra SMEM tile. Refine grids differ by a few configs (e.g. t8192 router 32 vs 27) because they are the same neighbourhood rule centred on each side's own winner. The ONLY asymmetry in valid configs is the 7-config SMEM bar on the fused w13 side, which is a real property of the kernel and is reported explicitly rather than hidden. All counts in rows[*].grid_sizes; full tune_tables recorded (148/143 router, 97/93 w13 entries at t8192).

3) SQ_MODE is a fused-side-only knob, so including it in the grid would have made the fused grid 4x the unfused grid. Resolved with a separate, fully-recorded pre-study at prefill_t2048 (32 entries in sq_mode_study.table), compared only over configs where every mode compiled, then held FIXED (mode 1, tile-accumulate, for both families) so the two search grids stay the same size.

4) The unfused side was given two extras it cannot get on the fused side, both of which can only help the baseline: an independent 152-config search over the RMSNorm kernel's own space (F3's tuned kernel, reused not rewritten), and a joint chain re-tune over top-3 GEMM x top-3 norm configs timed as the real two-kernel chain.

5) The SMEM pre-filter num_stages*2*BLOCK_K*(BLOCK_M+BLOCK_N) UNDER-estimates what MACA allocates (BM128 BN256 BK32 s2 predicted 49152 B, Triton reports 81920). A few configs therefore fail at launch; autotune records them rather than aborting, and the filter is applied identically to both sides.

6) The router GEMM never approaches its roofline on EITHER side at decode (43-60 GB/s), because N=256 yields only 8-128 CTAs on 104 CUs. Split-K was deliberately not implemented — it needs either a zeroing launch or a reduction launch, which would dominate at these sizes. This handicaps both sides equally and does not flip any sign (fusion loses by 30% there), but the decode absolute numbers are not production-grade.

7) The split-out norm kernel is bit-exact vs the reference at decode (0.00e+00) but 2.4-2.6e-03 at prefill, because the tuner picks a multi-pass BLOCK_N=1024/2048 mapping whose fp32 summation order moves rstd by ~1 bf16 ulp. That is baseline variation, not fusion error.

8) A first full run was aborted ~20 min in after the fused router showed a 55% instruction cost; a focused probe (scratchpad/f11/sqprobe.py) added the tensor-core and second-load SQ modes before relaunching. The delivered results come entirely from the relaunched run. The probe's w13 rows used a 32-expert weight (compute-bound proxy) and favoured the tensor-core mode; the in-benchmark pre-study on the real 256-expert weight does not, and that discrepancy is documented rather than papered over.

result.family: F4/F5 — (ResAdd +) RMSNorm + Router GEMM (+ FUSE_TOPK sigmoid/top-8)
result.verdict: NEGATIVE — do not fuse the router GEMM into the normalization on C500/Triton 3.0. Both #4 and #5 regress at every regime (0.21x-0.68x, i.e. 14-47% of the latency-aware roofline ceiling); FUSE_TOPK is strictly worse than plain fusion everywhere. The hardware premise was correct: W_gate (3.0 MB) does live in the 8 MB L2 and the stand-alone Triton router GEMM is compute-bound at 76.1 TF/s (71% of the 107 TF/s Triton ceiling) at T=8192, which is why the model predicted up to 1.97x. The failure is in the compiler. Attribution (all three LOG-10 diagnostics, per regime, in the JSON): (i) NOT registers — fused 140 regs / 18432 B SMEM vs the bare GEMM's 130 / 32768, zero spills, nothing barred by the SMEM ceiling (unlike F6); (ii) NOT traffic — pointing the activation input at a stride-0 broadcast (100 MB -> 12 KB) saves only 0.124 ms of 0.807 (15%), and removing the x2 store saves 0.065 (8%), while at T=2048 those isolations are worth just 3-4%; (iii) it IS the GEMM's schedule collapsing — the same FLOPs run at 31.9 TF/s fused vs 76.1 TF/s bare. Net: the fused kernel pays 0.469 ms over the bare GEMM at T=8192 for work the stand-alone rmsnorm kernel (same reads, same store, same arithmetic, 883 GB/s) does in 0.228 ms — normalization fused into a GEMM mainloop costs 2.1x what it costs in its own kernel (3.8x at T=2048). This is LOG-10 §1's F1 codegen cliff in a stronger, in-mainloop form, and it is now the third family it explains. Cross-config timings confirm neither side is under-tuned: each kernel is ~1.5x slower on the other's winning config. At decode the fused kernel additionally has only the expert dimension to parallelize over (each E-split redoes the whole norm), and FUSE_TOPK forbids that split entirely, leaving 1-16 CTAs on 104 CUs — hence the flat ~0.42 ms across T=1..256. Production recommendation: keep three launches, use F3's fused add_rmsnorm (a real 1.25x win) and call the vendor BLAS for the router GEMM (0.193 ms at t8192 vs our best Triton 0.338 and vs the fused kernel's 0.807).
result.issues: TWO SILENT WRONG-ANSWER CODEGEN BUGS IN MACA TRITON 3.0, both found only because every config of every variant is numerically screened against the fp32 reference before entering a timing grid (screen() in the bench). (1) A row-wise (axis=1) tl.max/tl.argmax over a tl.dot ACCUMULATOR returns a per-warp partial result whenever the mma tile spans more than one warp-row: BLOCK_M=16 ok at 4/8/16 warps, BLOCK_M=32 ok only at 4 warps, BLOCK_M=64 wrong at every warp count (probe: scratchpad/f04/t6.py; the accumulator itself is always correct — store it and reduce the reload and it is right). This rejects 23-24 of the 48 offered FUSE_TOPK configs in every regime and hard-caps the top-k fusion at 16-row tiles. A second form: broadcasting a reduced [BLOCK_M] vector back into a [BLOCK_M,8] tile after a dot returns garbage (ids=-1, weights=nan) even at BLOCK_M=16 — worked around by writing the 8 winners out one vector at a time and re-reading them; the stand-alone top-8 kernel runs the identical epilogue so both sides pay it. (2) num_warps=16 with BLOCK_M=16/BLOCK_K=32 produces completely wrong logits (rel_err ~1.0) in the fused kernel but is correct in the stand-alone GEMM where the A tile is loaded rather than computed; BLOCK_M=128 with NORM_BK=256 corrupts x2 (rel_err 0.92). METHODOLOGICAL WARNING for the rest of the study: a 2e-2 tolerance on top-k WEIGHTS accepts every one of these miscompiles — with norm_topk_prob on, a completely wrong expert selection still yields weights within 1-10% of 2.5/8=0.3125, and if W_gate is initialised too large the sigmoid scores saturate at 1.0 and a wrong router becomes numerically invisible. This bench initialises W_gate at 1/sqrt(H), checks the IDS not just the weights, and uses 2e-3 on weights / 8e-3 on activations (one bf16 ULP is 3.9e-3). FAIRNESS NOTE: grids are 80 (router GEMM) + 58 (norm) = 138 configs for the unfused #5 side vs 160 for the fused side (fused_grid = gemm_grid x {NORM_BK tied, NORM_BK widened}); the fused side deliberately gets MORE, since it is the side under suspicion, and each unfused chain additionally gets a 9-18 combination joint chain re-tune. NORM_BK (pass-1's own k-tile) had to be added mid-study: without it the fused side was rigged, running 96-192 sequential cross-lane reductions per row where the stand-alone norm kernel runs 3; it is worth up to -29% on some shapes and is chosen in 11 of the 20 winning fused configs, but it did not change the verdict. SCOPED OUT AND NOT BUILT: split-K with atomic_add on the fp32 logits, which would raise both sides' absolute decode numbers (the router GEMV is limited to 256/BLOCK_E CTAs) but cannot be combined with FUSE_TOPK and does not change a 1.00-1.17x decode ceiling. Compile time is ~6 s per config on this backend; the definitive run took ~2.5 h wall for 633 unique compiles plus timing.

result.verdict:
WORTH DOING — wins at all 5 regimes (1.147x-1.204x), capturing 73-102% of the 1.20x byte-saving ceiling; 99%/102% at the two prefill regimes where it is bandwidth-saturated at 1.48 TB/s. Second family after #3 to actually saturate its roofline, and the only one that wins at both decode and prefill.

MECHANISM (two different ones, which is why the curve is non-monotonic 1.175->1.181->1.147->1.204->1.198): at decode the win is launch-count (second launch costs ~1.4-2.8 us on a ~16 us base); at prefill it is pure bytes. decode_bs256 is the crossover trough where neither is at full strength (860 GB/s = 58% of the kernel's own prefill bandwidth, plus a still-significant fixed launch floor) — confirmed structural, the dip survives at p10, p50 and p90.

ATTRIBUTION (LOG-10 technique applied even though nothing regressed): fused costs +2..+4 registers vs merge-only (52-54 vs 50), ZERO spills, no SMEM pressure (no tl.dot). Stride-0-broadcast residual isolates cost: at prefill_t8192 the extra input costs 0.0586 ms of DRAM (86% of the 0.068 ms the roofline predicts) against 0.0054 ms of instructions (0.8% of kernel time) — the exact INVERSE of F1's codegen cliff. fused = merge_only + residual_read to within 2% everywhere.

FAIRNESS: one kernel source, DO_MERGE/DO_RESADD constexpr flags. Fused and unfused outputs are BITWISE IDENTICAL at every regime (asserted). 3646 trials, 0 compile failures: fused 1188, unfused 2458 (its two kernels over the same 174-config coarse generator + matching refines, PLUS a joint chain re-tune that only helps the baseline). Full TuneResult.table for all 5 regimes x 4 searches recorded in the JSON, plus the diagnostics.

TWO NULL RESULTS: (a) the 3-D slab mapping (KVEC=1, load [ROWS,8,BLOCK_N] and tl.sum(axis=1)) never wins the merge at any regime — the plain loop with an fp32 accumulator beats it every time; (b) dropping the intermediate bf16 rounding is free but buys almost nothing (final store rounding dominates), contrary to my expectation.

SURPRISES: a SINGLE warp (64 threads, BLOCK_N=256) wins prefill_t8192; unrolled static_range wins at decode but rolled tl.range wins at prefill; persistent grid essentially never wins; measured 1.48 TB/s exceeds traffic.py's 1.30 TB/s constant because this kernel is 9R:1W (the two existing calibration figures bracket it correctly, so the model under-predicts absolute time 12% while getting the ratio exactly right).

CEILING EXCURSION INVESTIGATED: prefill_t2048's 1.204x is 0.3% above the 1.20x ceiling. Not an error — byte ratio is exactly 1.200 and achieved bandwidths match (1383 vs 1378 GB/s); the excess is one saved launch (+0.9% available on a 0.18 ms kernel), consistent at p10/p50/p90.

REFERENCE LINES: no GEMM, so no vendor-BLAS line. torch eager is 3.9-9.5x slower. torch.compile/inductor DOES work on this MACA backend and is numerically correct, but is 1.1-3.8x slower than the hand kernel; byte arithmetic at t8192 (measured 2.61 ms vs 0.82 ms fully-fused ideal vs 3.00 ms with the fp32 promotion materialized) says inductor reduces over a 1.6 GB fp32 temporary. Inductor is a reasonable choice at decode_bs1 (8% off) and a bad one at prefill. Cross-check: my merge_only (0.6129 ms at t8192) is faster than F8/F9's port of sglang's _moe_sum_reduce_kernel (0.6444 ms) while doing strictly more work (it also applies the fp32 routing weight), so the baseline is not a straw man.

CAVEAT THAT SHOULD GOVERN THE ENGINEERING DECISION: sglang does NOT ship the standalone residual-add kernel this baseline uses. Verified in the shipped source (glm4_moe.py + layers/communicator.py): the decoder layer carries (hidden_states, residual) as a pair and the post-MoE add is absorbed by the NEXT layer's fused_add_rmsnorm, i.e. #10 and #3 compete for the same add. Row-pass counts for the whole tail: sglang today 13, the baseline measured here 14, F10-fused 12, F10+F3 fused together 11. So the measured 1.20x is exactly the comparison specified, but the actionable end-to-end number is 13/12 = 1.083x. RECOMMENDED NEXT: the triple fusion merge+resadd+rmsnorm = 11 passes = 1.18x end-to-end, subsuming both #3 and #10; it needs no atomics, no SMEM, no tl.dot, ~55 registers, and both parents hit ~100% of their ceilings.

VS F8/F9 (they attack the same reduction from the GEMM side): they are not measuring the same thing and reading the columns as competitors is a mistake — F10's 1.20x is 20% of a 0.68 ms tail; F8's 0.87x is -13% of a 20.4 ms GEMM. In absolute ms at prefill_t8192, F10 SAVES 0.135 ms while F8 COSTS 3.0 ms. At prefill: do F10, not F8. At decode both are inside the layer's noise, but F10 is bit-exact whereas F8's bf16 atomics cost ~1 bit (rel_err 3.5e-3 -> 8.8e-3). F8_token_major, the only variant that truly eliminates F10's kernel, is a decode_bs1-only curiosity (0.021x at prefill), so that path is closed on this hardware.
result.issues:
One measurement was rejected and the probe rewritten rather than the outlier deleted: the first (non-interleaved) attribution run reported a 2.86 ms residual DRAM cost at decode_bs256 for a kernel whose total runtime is 0.0366 ms — internally impossible. glm52/bench/diag_f10_merge_resadd.py now times all four variants in an interleaved round-robin over 3 passes, min-of-medians (same remedy as LOG-05 section 8); the re-run reproduces the clean pass to within 3% on every cell and the pathological cell is gone. The headline fused-vs-unfused numbers come from the bench's own bench_chain and were never affected.

Absolute p10-p90 spread is wide at decode (19-22% at decode_bs1, 9-13% at decode_bs32) because a ~20 us kernel is Python-launch-bound. The jitter is correlated across the two sides, so the RATIO is stable: every regime's speedup at p10 and p90 agrees with the p50 headline to within +/-0.03x and no interval touches 1.0x. Table is in LOG section 6.

Two grid asymmetries, both stated in the log and both favouring the baseline: (1) resadd_only ignores the KVEC/UNROLL knobs (no top-k loop), so ~half its 174 coarse configs are behavioural duplicates that merely get timed twice — extra samples for the unfused side, no reduction in distinct mappings for the fused side; (2) refine-grid sizes vary 52-72 across variants purely because a winner at the edge of the BLOCK_N/ROWS/num_warps ladders has fewer +/-1 neighbours (same generator, same rule). All n_tried values are recorded per regime per search.

Reported unfused timings use the joint chain re-tune, not the sum of independently-tuned kernels. This matters a lot: at decode the naive sum overstates the baseline by 40-67% (0.0315 vs 0.0189 ms at decode_bs1), which would have manufactured a fake ~1.96x.

Benchmark wall time was ~60 min on a cold Triton cache (MACA compiles ~4 s each dominate the first regime), ~5 min warm. Per-regime checkpoints in results/_f10_merge_resadd_ckpt/ are reused on restart, so re-running the bench as-is will replay from checkpoint rather than re-tune; delete that directory to force a fresh run.
